newsitem.title: GERMANY: SPD attacks Bonn's resistance to EU jobs plan.
newsitem.headline: SPD attacks Bonn's resistance to EU jobs plan.

text.p: Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD) on Wednesday attacked the government for failing to support a proposed European-wide initiative to create employment.

SPD chief Oskar Lafontaine said such resistance threatened the long-term stability of European unity. "Europe must be a Europe in which its citizens have access to employment," Lafontaine said in a parliamentary speech.

He added that job creation policies should be anchored "right at the centre" of the push towards monetary union, which so far had concentrated more on assuring the convergence of other economic criteria.

The SPD and the newly-elected French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin had directly before the left-wing victory in France launched a plan that among other things would coordinate more training opportunities across the continent and iron existing tax imbalances that were creating employment blackspots.

Lafontaine in parliament further cited the expansion of European transport networks, a much-favoured project of the European left, as one clear opportunity to create lasting and valuable employment across the continent.

He described the current position of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's government that employment policies should be handled nationally as a sign of "dangerous cynicism towards other European states" that were pushing for more coordination in the area.
